g.text: - Primary capabilities — What operations must this system support?

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Rules and completion — What conditions define success, failure, or when the system stops or transitions state?

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Error handling — How should the system respond when inputs or actions are invalid?

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Scope boundaries — What areas are in scope (core logic, business rules) and

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: what areas are explicitly out (UI, storage, networking, concurrency, extensibility)?

g.text: - If something maintains changing state or enforces rules, it likely deserves to be its own entity.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - If it’s just information attached to something else, it’s probably just a field on another class.

g.text: Modern production systems favor composition over inheritance, simple state over deep hierarchies, and pragmatism over pattern worship

g.text: For each entity, you'll answer two questions:

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: State - What does this class need to remember to enforce the requirements?

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Behavior - What does this class need to do, in terms of operations or queries?

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - What information does it need to keep in memory to satisfy those responsibilities?

g.text: - Design principles guide your decision making to create clean, extensible, and maintainable code

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - When you're designing a class or choosing between patterns, pick the straightforward approach.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: If you can solve the problem with a simple conditional instead of a strategy pattern, do tha

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - When you find yourself writing the same logic in multiple places, pull it into one place.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: If three classes all validate email addresses the same way, create a shared validation method.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - This principle doesn't mean "never think ahead" - it means don't build ahead. Design with

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: extension in mind, but only implement what's needed now.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Different parts of your code should handle different responsibilities, and they shouldn't know about each other's internals.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Your UI layer shouldn't contain business logic.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Your business logic shouldn't know how data is stored.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Your data access layer shouldn't format strings for display.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Also called the principle of least knowledge.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: A method should only talk to its immediate friends, not reach through objects to access distant parts of the system.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: If you see code like order.getCustomer().getAddress().getZipCode(), that's violating the Law of Demeter.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: A class should have one reason to change. If a class mixes multiple concerns, split them. This is the foundation of good class

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Classes should be open for extension but closed for modification.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: You should be able to add new behavior without changing existing code.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: This usually means using interfaces or abstract classes so you can add new implementations without touching the original code.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: If your code uses a parent class or interface, it should be able to use any subclass without knowing which specific subclass it is.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: The subclass can add new behavior, but it can't remove or break behavior that the parent promised

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Prefer small, focused interfaces over large, general-purpose ones.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Don't force classes to implement methods they don't need.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: If a class only needs two methods from an interface with ten methods, that interface is too big

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Dependency Inversion states that your code should depend on abstractions, not concrete implementations

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Encapsulation means keeping an object’s data private and letting the object control how that data is used.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: You interact with it through simple methods instead of reaching in and changing its internal details yourself.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Abstraction means exposing only what's essential and hiding implementation details behind clear interfaces.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: You define what something can do without revealing how it does it.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Polymorphism is what replaces if (type == "credit") or switch (vehicleType) statements.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Instead of checking types, you call the same method and let each object handle itself.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Different objects respond to the same action in their own way.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Python doesn't support compile-time polymorphism because it is dynamically typed.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Method names must be unique within a class, and function selection based on argument types cannot be done at compile time since types are only known at runtime.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Python supports multiple inheritance by allowing a class to inherit from multiple base classes.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: When there is ambiguity about which method to call, Python uses the MRO, calculated using C3 linearization, to determine the lookup order.
